The AI coding tool your engineering team uses just became a $60 billion strategic asset inside a space and infrastructure company.

SpaceX filed to acquire Cursor in a $60 billion all-stock deal on June 16. Cursor currently generates approximately $4 billion in annualized revenue — $2.6 billion of that from enterprise customers. A joint AI model trained on xAI's Colossus infrastructure will ship inside both Cursor and a new product called Grok Build. Closing is expected Q3 2026.

This is not a developer tools acquisition. This is the convergence of AI compute infrastructure, frontier model training, and the code editor as a platform. SpaceX gains an enterprise software distribution channel with deep workflow integration. Cursor gains access to one of the largest private AI compute clusters on the planet.

For CTOs: the IDE is no longer a neutral utility. It is becoming a vertically integrated AI platform tied to specific model ecosystems and compute infrastructure. The tool your developers write code in will increasingly determine which AI models they access, which training data improves those models, and which infrastructure stack your organization depends on.

Nasdaq-100 inclusion is expected around July 7. Five of six analysts covering the deal recommend buying. The market is pricing in a scenario more bullish than Street consensus.
